chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding false testimony: if the item is still in existence, it is returned to its owner; and if it is no longer in existence, the witness is liable for compensation equal to the value of what was destroyed from the man's wealth.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on false testimony when the disputed property is lost versus when it is still available?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *daman* (financial compensation) for false witnesses, distinguishing between restitution of the specific asset if it remains intact and monetary compensation for its value if destroyed. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the tangible economic consequences of perjury, ensuring that the victim is made whole regardless of the item's fate. This ruling underscores the gravity of *shahadat al-zur* not merely as a procedural error but as a direct cause of financial loss requiring precise legal redress.
